title: Infection control — standard precautions
definition: CDC standard precautions applied to all patients regardless of diagnosis.
keyPoints: Hand hygiene before/after every patient contact
PPE based on anticipated exposure (gloves, gown, mask, eyewear)
Safe sharps handling — no recapping
Cough etiquette
Environmental cleaning
pearls: Alcohol-based hand rub if hands not visibly soiled; soap+water if soiled.
clinicalContext: Nurse caring for multiple patients in a ward.
nursingPriority: Perform hand hygiene at 5 moments (WHO): before patient contact, before aseptic task, after body fluid exposure risk, after patient contact, after contact with patient surroundings.

title: Code of ethics — ICN/INC
definition: Ethical guidelines for nursing practice.
keyPoints: ICN code: promote health, prevent illness, restore health, alleviate suffering
INC 2018: 4 elements — nurse and patient/individual, practice, profession, co-workers
Pillars: autonomy, beneficence, non-maleficence, justice, fidelity, veracity
Confidentiality protected except by law
clinicalContext: Patient refuses blood transfusion on religious grounds despite severe anemia.
nursingPriority: Respect autonomy after verifying informed refusal, document, involve multi-disciplinary team including ethics committee.

topic: Lines and tubes — suctioning, ETT, NG, tracheostomy, CVP
title: Lines and tubes — suctioning, ETT, NG, tracheostomy, CVP
definition: Routine care of commonly encountered tubes/lines.
keyPoints: Suctioning: pre-oxygenate 100% O2, sterile technique, <15 sec, negative pressure 80-150 adult
ETT: confirm bilateral breath sounds, CXR position 2-4 cm above carina, cuff 20-30 cmH2O
NG: verify pH <5.5 aspirate or X-ray
Tracheostomy: inner cannula care q8h, stoma cleaning, humidification
CVP: dress q7d transparent/q2d gauze, chlorhexidine scrub
pearls: Never instill saline as a routine in closed suction.
clinicalContext: Patient on ventilator needs suctioning for thick secretions.
nursingPriority: Pre-oxygenate to 100% x 30 sec, sterile technique, insert without suction, apply suction while withdrawing <15 sec, reassess SpO2.

topic: Oxygen therapy devices and flow rates
title: Oxygen therapy devices and flow rates
definition: Oxygen delivery devices and FiO2 achieved.
keyPoints: Nasal cannula: 1-6 L/min → 24-44% FiO2 (rule: 4% per L)
Simple mask: 5-10 L/min → 40-60%
Venturi: precise 24-60% (blue 24, white 28, yellow 35, red 40, green 60)
Non-rebreather: 10-15 L → 90-100%
Must humidify at flow >4 L/min
pearls: Target SpO2 88-92% in COPD, 94-98% in most adults.
clinicalContext: COPD patient needs precise FiO2 28% due to CO2 retention risk.
nursingPriority: Apply Venturi mask with white/28% adapter, flow as labeled on device (typically 4 L), monitor SpO2 88-92%.

title: Blood transfusion and sampling
definition: Safe transfusion practice.
keyPoints: Bedside double-check: patient ID, blood group/Rh, crossmatch, product expiry
Start within 30 min of release from blood bank, complete within 4 h
Vitals baseline, 15 min, hourly
Use 0.9% saline only in same line
Transfusion reactions: acute hemolytic, febrile non-hemolytic, allergic, TRALI, TACO
pearls: Anti-D within 72 h for Rh-negative who receives Rh+ blood.
clinicalContext: Patient starts chills, lower back pain, fever 15 min into transfusion.
nursingPriority: STOP transfusion, keep line open with NS, notify physician, send blood bag + tubing + patient blood/urine for workup — suspect acute hemolytic reaction.

title: IV fluids — types and indications
definition: Crystalloids and colloids for fluid resuscitation/maintenance.
keyPoints: Isotonic: NS 0.9%, RL, Plasmalyte — resuscitation
Hypotonic: 0.45% NaCl, D5W (becomes hypotonic after dextrose metabolized) — maintenance
Hypertonic: 3% NaCl, D10, D25 — hyponatremia/hypoglycemia
Colloids: albumin, hydroxyethyl starch (avoid in sepsis), gelatin
Maintenance formula 4-2-1: 100/50/20 mL/kg/d
nursingPriority: 4-2-1 rule: 100 mL/h for first 10 kg, 50 for next 10, 20 for rest → ~110 mL/h of NS or RL.

title: Oral care (unconscious patient)
definition: Prevention of VAP and aspiration in unconscious/ventilated patients.
keyPoints: Side-lying or head turned
Chlorhexidine 0.12% oral rinse BD (VAP bundle)
Soft toothbrush or swab q4-6h
Suction ready; small amounts of fluid
Moisten lips with petroleum jelly
clinicalContext: ICU patient intubated needs oral care.
nursingPriority: Position side-lying, suction prepared, use soft swab with CHG 0.12%, clean tongue to reduce biofilm, moisten lips.

title: Airway management
definition: Open airway and ventilate effectively.
keyPoints: Head-tilt chin-lift (no trauma); jaw thrust if C-spine
OPA (size: corner of mouth to angle of mandible) — only if unconscious, no gag
NPA (size: tip of nose to tragus) — for semi-conscious
Bag-valve-mask: 1 breath per 5-6 sec adult, 1 per 3 sec child
LMA, ETT as escalation
nursingPriority: Head-tilt chin-lift, insert OPA sized mouth corner to mandibular angle, check breathing, bag-valve-mask if inadequate.

topic: IV cannula — gauges and colour coding
title: IV cannula — gauges and colour coding
definition: Peripheral IV cannula sizes by gauge.
keyPoints: 14G orange: trauma/rapid infusion
16G grey: trauma, surgery
18G green: blood, contrast
20G pink: routine IV, blood
22G blue: children, thin veins
24G yellow: neonates/very thin
nursingPriority: Insert 14G or 16G in antecubital; 2 large-bore for rapid fluid/blood resuscitation.

title: Cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR)
definition: High-quality CPR per AHA 2020 adult guidelines.
keyPoints: Compression rate 100-120/min, depth 5-6 cm, full recoil
Ratio 30:2 (one rescuer) until advanced airway
Minimize interruptions <10 sec
Switch compressors q2 min
Shockable: VF/pulseless VT → defibrillate, then resume CPR
Child: 15:2 if 2 rescuers; depth 1/3 AP diameter
pearls: Hands-only CPR if untrained or unwilling to ventilate.
clinicalContext: Adult collapse in ward, no pulse, no breathing.
nursingPriority: Start chest compressions immediately 100-120/min depth 5-6 cm, call code, attach AED, shock if VF/VT, continue 30:2 with bag-mask.

title: Drug calculation basics
definition: Common formulas for dose and rate calculation.
keyPoints: Dose: (desired/have) x volume
Drops/min: (volume x drop factor) / time (min); macrodrip 15 or 20 gtt/mL, microdrip 60 gtt/mL
Pediatric dose: mg/kg or m2 BSA
Infusion: mL/h = mg/min desired × 60 / concentration
clinicalContext: Give 1 g cefazolin in 100 mL NS over 30 min using 20 gtt/mL set.
nursingPriority: Drops/min = (100 x 20) / 30 = 67 gtt/min.

title: Bandaging
definition: Techniques for wound support/compression/immobilization.
keyPoints: Types: spiral, reverse spiral, figure-of-8, spica, recurrent
Principles: distal to proximal, even tension, distal pulse check
Assess: colour, warmth, movement, sensation distal to bandage
nursingPriority: Figure-of-8 from foot distal to leg proximal, 50% overlap, check capillary refill and toe colour after.

title: Patient positioning
definition: Therapeutic and functional positioning.
keyPoints: Semi-Fowler (30°): respiratory, cardiac, NG feeding
Fowler (45-60°): dyspnea
High-Fowler (>60°): CHF, severe dyspnea
Trendelenburg: hypotension (historical — limited evidence)
Left lateral: pregnancy (venous return), late-pregnancy emergency
Prone: ARDS (>=12 h/day)
Sim: enema
Orthopneic: COPD
nursingPriority: Prone positioning for >=12 h/day, protect pressure points, secure all lines, airway clearance.

topic: Assessment scales — GCS, Braden, Norton, FLACC
title: Assessment scales — GCS, Braden, Norton, FLACC
definition: Common assessment tools.
keyPoints: GCS: E4V5M6 max 15, coma <=8
Braden: pressure risk (<=18 at risk; lower = higher risk)
Norton: pressure risk (<=14 at risk)
FLACC: pediatric pain (Face, Legs, Activity, Cry, Consolability 0-10)
Numeric pain 0-10
Wong-Baker faces: pediatric pain
nursingPriority: Assess pain with FLACC; sum 0-10; >=4 intervene with analgesic.

title: Enema — types and procedure
definition: Fluid instilled into rectum for evacuation or medication.
keyPoints: Cleansing: tap water, NS, soap-suds
Retention: oil (100-200 mL), medicated
Return-flow (Harris): air distension relief
Position: left lateral Sim
Tube insertion 7-10 cm adult, 2.5-4 cm child
Height: 30-45 cm above anus
nursingPriority: Left lateral Sim, lubricate tip, insert 7-10 cm, allow fluid to flow by gravity 30-45 cm height, encourage retention 5-10 min.

title: Care of colostomy patient
definition: Care of surgically created bowel opening.
keyPoints: Types: ileostomy (liquid output, skin excoriation risk), transverse/descending/sigmoid colostomy (more formed)
Stoma: pink/red moist; assess for necrosis (dark), retraction, prolapse
Bag change when 1/3 full; skin barrier
High-fiber diet for constipation, avoid gas-producing foods
Body image support
nursingPriority: Assess stoma colour (pink/red healthy), measure output, empty when 1/3 full, apply skin barrier, provide psychological support.

title: Medication administration — rights and routes
definition: Medication safety framework.
keyPoints: 10 rights: patient, drug, dose, route, time, documentation, reason, response, education, right to refuse
3 checks: when taking from cabinet, preparing, administering
Routes: PO, SL, buccal, SC, IM, IV, ID, PR, topical, inhaled, transdermal
clinicalContext: About to give metformin 500 mg PO to patient.
nursingPriority: Check patient ID with 2 identifiers (name + DOB/MRN), right drug/dose/route/time, educate, document.

topic: Patient safety — SPEAK UP and NPSG
title: Patient safety — SPEAK UP and NPSG
definition: System and communication strategies to prevent harm.
keyPoints: NPSG (Joint Commission 2024): identify correctly, communicate effectively (SBAR), medications safely, alarms, prevent infections, falls, suicide
SPEAK UP: Speak up, Pay attention, Educate, Advocate, Know meds, Use quality facility, Participate
SBAR: Situation, Background, Assessment, Recommendation
nursingPriority: Use SBAR: state situation (post-op day 1), background (diabetic, CKD), assessment (stable but pain 7/10), recommendation (PRN analgesia q4h).

title: Crutch walking — gaits
definition: Ambulation techniques with crutches.
keyPoints: 4-point: maximum support, slowest (R crutch → L foot → L crutch → R foot)
2-point: faster, partial weight (R crutch + L foot together, L crutch + R foot)
3-point: non-weight bearing leg — crutches first, then good leg
Swing-through: both legs together, most advanced
Stairs: good leg first going up, bad leg first going down
clinicalContext: Post-ORIF right femur patient, non-weight-bearing right.
nursingPriority: Teach 3-point gait: both crutches forward + injured leg, then hop good leg through; "good up, bad down" for stairs.

title: Restraint — types and care
definition: Mechanical or chemical restriction of movement — last resort.
keyPoints: Types: physical (wrist, vest, mitt), chemical (sedatives), environmental (locked unit)
Indications: imminent harm to self/others; all alternatives failed
Physician order within 1 h; renew q4h adult, q1h child
Assess q15 min: circulation, skin, hydration, toileting, ROM
Quick-release knot — never square knot
clinicalContext: Agitated post-ICU patient pulling at IV lines.
nursingPriority: Try de-escalation, then least-restrictive restraint if needed, physician order within 1 h, assess q15 min, release q2h for ROM/toileting.

title: Health assessment
definition: Systematic head-to-toe patient assessment.
keyPoints: Sequence: inspection → palpation → percussion → auscultation (abdomen: inspect → auscultate → percuss → palpate)
Vital signs baseline
Subjective (history) + objective (exam) data
Focus assessment for chief complaint
Document using body system approach
nursingPriority: Take vitals, collect history, perform head-to-toe in IPPA order (except abdomen), document findings, report abnormalities.

title: Urinary catheter care
definition: CAUTI prevention in indwelling catheters.
keyPoints: Insert only when necessary; remove as early as possible
Sterile insertion, closed drainage
Secure catheter to thigh to prevent traction
Keep bag below bladder, never on floor
Peri-care BD with soap and water
Never disconnect unless indicated
nursingPriority: Daily assessment of need, perineal care BD, ensure unobstructed drainage, bag below bladder, document output; plan removal ASAP.

title: Chest tube care
definition: Water-seal drainage system.
keyPoints: 3 chambers: collection, water-seal, suction control
Normal: bubbling in suction chamber; tidaling in water-seal with respiration
Continuous bubbling in water-seal = air leak
Keep below chest level; no kinks; never clamp >1 h (tension pneumothorax risk)
Milking/stripping not routine
pearls: Bubbling in water-seal during expiration only is normal.
nursingPriority: Keep drainage unit below chest, monitor tidaling, report continuous bubbling (air leak), measure output hourly, never clamp during transport unless directed.

title: Thoracentesis
definition: Needle aspiration of pleural fluid.
keyPoints: Position: upright, leaning on table with arms resting
Site: 2 ICS below fluid level, above rib to avoid neurovascular bundle
<1.5 L/session to avoid re-expansion pulmonary edema
Complications: pneumothorax, bleeding, infection
nursingPriority: Position sitting leaning forward, assist with aspiration above rib, monitor for cough/dyspnea (pneumothorax), send fluid to lab, CXR post-procedure.

title: Lumbar puncture — procedure and position
definition: Sampling CSF via subarachnoid space L3-L4 or L4-L5.
keyPoints: Position: lateral recumbent knees-to-chest or sitting leaning forward
Site: iliac crest line = L4 body
Contraindications: raised ICP, skin infection, coagulopathy
Post-LP: bed rest supine 4-6 h, hydration to reduce headache
clinicalContext: Suspected meningitis, no signs of raised ICP.
nursingPriority: Position lateral with knees-to-chest, prep L3-L4 site, assist with sterile technique, label tubes sequentially (typically 1-cell count, 2-biochem, 3-microbio, 4-spare), bed rest after.

title: Pulmonary artery catheter
definition: Swan-Ganz catheter measures right heart pressures and cardiac output.
keyPoints: Normal CVP 2-8 mmHg; PA pressure 15-30/8-15; PCWP 6-12 (reflects LVEDP)
PCWP elevated in LV failure; CVP in RV failure/volume overload
Complications: arrhythmia, PA rupture, infection, thrombus
Less used now due to complications
clinicalContext: ICU patient with unclear fluid status.
nursingPriority: Ensure transducer at phlebostatic axis (4th ICS mid-axillary), zero regularly, monitor waveform, report dampening (thrombus) or high pressures.

title: Pressure ulcer stages
definition: See Surgery-17; same staging.
keyPoints: Risk assessment: Braden (6 subscales, total 6-23; <=18 at risk)
Prevention: turn q2h, pressure-redistributing mattress, skin inspection daily, moisture management, nutrition
nursingPriority: Turn q2h, air/foam mattress, heel offload, skin assessment per shift, nutritional review, moisturize dry skin.

title: Vital signs
definition: Baseline physiologic parameters.
keyPoints: Child varies by age: infant HR 100-160, RR 30-60; toddler HR 80-130; school-age 70-110
Apical HR for 1 min in children and irregular rhythms
Orthostatic: drop >20/10 or rise HR >20
nursingPriority: Document expected newborn: HR 120-160, RR 30-60, axillary T 36.5-37.5.

title: Spill management — BMW
definition: BMW Rules 2016 colour-coded waste and spill handling.
keyPoints: Yellow: infectious, anatomical, chemical, pharmaceutical
Red: contaminated recyclable plastics (gloves, tubing, catheters)
White: sharps (translucent)
Blue: glassware, metallic body implants
Spill: contain, disinfect with 1% sodium hypochlorite 10 min, clean inside-out, document, report
nursingPriority: Wear PPE, cover with absorbent paper, apply 1% NaOCl for 10 min, wipe from outside toward center, discard in yellow bag, document.

title: Needle stick injury — PEP
definition: Occupational exposure to blood-borne pathogens.
keyPoints: Immediate: allow to bleed freely, wash with soap+water (no scrubbing), don't suck or squeeze
Report within 2 h
Source + worker testing for HIV, HBV, HCV
HIV PEP within 2 h (best) up to 72 h: tenofovir + emtricitabine + dolutegravir x28 d
HBV: vaccine + HBIg if unvaccinated
pearls: Window period for HIV antibodies ~6 wk.
clinicalContext: Nurse sustained needle stick from HIV+ patient.
nursingPriority: Allow to bleed, wash with soap+water, report within 2 h, start PEP TDF+FTC+DTG within 2 h, test at 0/6 wk/3 mo/6 mo, counselling.
